alt: Two panels. Supervised learning: labelled squares and triangles are known and a new unknown item is assigned to one of the two groups. Unsupervised learning: unlabelled shapes are grouped into three clusters by similarity.
author: Balkiss.hamad

alt: A deep network with inputs at the bottom (an elephant, a kangaroo and a penguin) and labels at the top. Layers learn increasingly complex features, from short strokes to parts of an elephant. The feature layers are marked unsupervised learning and the whole stack, with the labels, is marked supervised learning.
author: Sven Behnke

alt: An autoencoder: the input layer X is squeezed by the encoder into a small code h, and the decoder expands the code into the output layer X prime.
author: Michela Massi

alt: A restricted Boltzmann machine: three visible units on the left and four hidden units on the right, with every visible unit joined to every hidden unit and no connections inside a layer.
author: Qwertyus

alt: A generative adversarial network: noise z goes into the generator, which makes a fake G(z); the discriminator receives the fake and a real sample x and decides whether the input is real or fake.
author: Zhang, Aston and Lipton, Zachary C. and Li, Mu and Smola, Alexander J.

alt: A convolutional neural network: a robot image is passed through convolution and subsampling layers that produce smaller and smaller feature maps, then a fully connected layer gives the output.
author: Aphex34

alt: A stack of layers h1, h2, h3 with weights w1, w2, w3 between them, trained upward from the input, and a top layer h4 that gives the recognized class.
author: Numiri

alt: A deep belief network: the visible layer at the bottom, hidden layers 1 and 2 above it joined by downward arrows only, and hidden layers 2 and 3 joined by two-way arrows at the top.
author: Qwertyus

alt: Rosenblatt's two figures: the organization of a biological brain, from retina to motor cortex, and the organization of a perceptron, from sensory points through association units to response units.
author: Rosenblatt, F.

alt: A biological neuron: inputs arrive at the dendrites, the cell body (soma) combines them, and the signal travels along the myelinated axon to the output terminals.
author: Egm4313.s12 (Prof. Loc Vu-Quoc)

alt: An artificial neuron: inputs x1 to xn are multiplied by weights, a summation unit adds them, and an activation function with a threshold gives the output.
author: Funcs

alt: The layer-by-layer structure of LeNet (28 by 28 image, 10 classes) and AlexNet (224 by 224 image, 1000 classes) with their convolution, pooling and dense layers.
author: Cmglee

alt: A perceptron: inputs i1 to in are multiplied by weights W1 to Wn, added, and passed through a function f to give the output o.
author: Mat the w at English Wikipedia

alt: A recurrent network drawn folded, with a loop on the hidden state h, and unfolded over time into a chain of hidden states h(t-1), h(t), h(t+1), each with its input x and output o.
author: fdeloche

alt: An LSTM unit between time steps: a memory cell c runs along the top, controlled by a forget gate, an input gate and an output gate, each a sigmoid or tanh box.
author: fdeloche

alt: A GRU unit between time steps with a reset gate R and an update gate Z acting on the hidden state h.
author: fdeloche

alt: A deep autoencoder: the input X passes through an encoder to a narrow code z, and the decoder rebuilds the output X prime from the code.
author: Chervinskii

alt: A radial basis function network: three input nodes feed four radial basis function nodes, whose outputs are combined with linear weights into one output y.
author: Leitisvatn

alt: Four stacked plots of sigmoid, ReLU, leaky ReLU and SiLU. In each plot a red curve is the function and a dashed orange curve is its slope. The sigmoid slope peaks at 0.25 and falls to almost zero at both ends; the ReLU slope is 0 for negative inputs and 1 for positive inputs.
author: CapeItalist

alt: A picture of a dog goes into a CNN, which gives scores 35.4 for cat, 38.1 for dog and -5.0 for horse. Softmax turns these into probabilities 0.06, 0.94 and 0.00.
author: Fschwarzentruber

alt: A training loop: a minibatch goes through a forward pass (compute predictions, compute loss) and a backward pass (compute gradients, update parameters), then the loop asks whether training has converged.
author: Alexis0Olson

alt: Loss against error from -4 to 4. The blue squared-error curve rises steeply, and the green Huber loss matches it near zero then continues as a straight line.
author: Qwertyus

alt: Log loss against predicted probability p from 0 to 1 for a true label of 1: the loss is very high near p = 0 and falls to 0 at p = 1.
author: Bfortuner

alt: Loss against predicted output for a target of 1. The binary cross-entropy curve rises steeply to above 2 as the output nears 0.1, while the mean-squared-error curve stays below 0.5.
author: M.Zkuba

alt: Hinge loss (blue, a straight line falling to zero at 1) and zero-one loss (green, a step from 1 to 0 at 0), plotted against the score.
author: Qwertyus
